text:
alex: Filing a customer report — CSV export from Console analytics shows header row only and S3 object 0 bytes when the query includes a filter tag set to <null>. Repro steps I have:
alex: 1) Console -> Analytics -> Exports
alex: 2) Select date range 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-14, segmentation by customer_tag, add filter customer_tag: "null" (explicit null filter), click Export CSV
alex: 3) UI shows 'Export ready', download link hits presigned S3 URL, file downloads but is 0 bytes.
maria: Can you paste the X-Export-ID or the link from the UI?
alex: export id = XEXP-20260314-9f8a
alex: Presigned GET returns: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  content-length: 0
  content-type: text/csv
  x-amz-request-id: 3ABCD1234EFG
  x-amz-id-2: ...
  date: Sun, 14 Mar 2026 18:22:10 GMT
alex: The export-service returns success and S3 put reported success in logs, but object size=0 in S3 console.
export-bot: export-service notice: export XEXP-20260314-9f8a completed, rows=124, archive=gs://redwood-exports/2026/03/14/XEXP-9f8a.csv, duration=9s
sam: Did customer_tag=null filter change the SQL? Maybe we accidentally generate a WHERE tag IS NULL that the csv-streamer mis-handles. Any stack traces?
alex: I captured export-service logs around the job: 
[worker-1] job=XEXP-9f8a status=started
[worker-1] job=XEXP-9f8a rows_streamed=124
[worker-1] job=XEXP-9f8a s3_put_response={"ETag":"\"abc123\"","ContentLength":0}
[worker-1] job=XEXP-9f8a status=completed

luis: ContentLength:0 in s3_put_response is the smoking gun. That means our upload call sent empty body. Could be an iterator exhaustion when segmenting by customer_tag with null bucket.
maria: Can you try a smaller range or same filter via the API (not Console) and attach curl + Authorization masked?
alex: Repro via API: 
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports?start=2026-03-01&end=2026-03-14&segment=customer_tag&filter=customer_tag:null" -o export.json
Response: 202 Accepted {"export_id":"XEXP-20260314-9f8a"}
Wait 10s then GET /exports/XEXP-20260314-9f8a/status -> completed
GET presigned url -> 200, zero bytes.

sam: Can you attach the worker logs with DEBUG enabled? Need to see csv_streamer/partition logic. Also check if gzip flag set.
alex: snippet from worker debug: 
DEBUG csv_streamer: partition_for_tag -> ["(null)"]
DEBUG csv_streamer: open_stream() -> StreamingBodyIterator()
DEBUG csv_streamer: for row in rows: yield row
DEBUG csv_streamer: rows consumed -> True
DEBUG s3_client: multipart_upload_complete -> parts=[]
DEBUG s3_client: put_object called with Body=<generator>, ContentEncoding=None
DEBUG s3_client: upload_stream finished
DEBUG s3_client: reported_content_length=0

luis: The parts=[] implies multipart flow kicked in but no parts were uploaded. Maybe the generator closed before first chunk. Could be a divide-by-zero in batch size when partition is only null values.
eng-oncall: Opening an internal incident and assigning to eng-runtime. Incident created: INC-20260314-87, priority P2. Please attach the full worker logs and the export job payload.
maria: Alex, can you paste the export job payload (without tokens)? Also which browser and region?
alex: payload: {"start":"2026-03-01","end":"2026-03-14","segment":"customer_tag","filters":[{"field":"customer_tag","op":"is","value":null}],"format":"csv"}
alex: Browser: Chrome 111 MacOS, region: us-west-2

sam: Quick mitigation: if the filter is null, fallback to SQL predicate "customer_tag IS NULL" explicitly in exporter and avoid the partitioning code path. But that's a code change. For support, can we suggest customers use 'customer_tag:"(unknown)"' alias?
luis: Temporary workaround for customers: avoid segmentation by customer_tag for queries that include a NULL filter, or run export via API with small date windows and concatenate. I'll draft a support KB.
export-bot: export-service notice: re-run job XEXP-20260314-9f8a attempted by user alex at 18:45:12, status=failed, error="upload zero-bytes to s3"

maria: Thanks — putting this into the support ticket and linking INC-20260314-87. Eng-runtime please prioritize a fix on the CSV streaming multipart path.
eng-oncall: Assigned to @sam and @luis. Next steps: reproduce in staging with null partition, run with debug, add guard to not enter multipart when first chunk is empty. ETA preliminary fix: 2-3 days.
alex: I'll follow up with the customer and give the workaround. Adding any additional logs here if needed. :thumbsup:
